Draft a methods paragraph for a fitted model

Source: R/report_methods.R
report_methods.Rd

Drafts the text that describes a model fitted with bmm() in the methods section of a paper: the model, the software and sampler settings, the priors, and the convergence diagnostics. The draft is meant to be edited, not pasted unread.

Usage

report_methods(fit, sections = c("model", "priors", "convergence"))

Arguments

fit

A bmmfit object returned by bmm(). It must contain posterior draws, so mock fits and fits made with chains = 0 or empty = TRUE are refused.

sections

The parts of the paragraph to draft, in the order they should appear: "model" (the model, the versions of bmm, brms, Stan, the backend and R, and the sampler settings), "priors" (the sentences of prior_info() with format = "text") and "convergence" (the sentence of report_convergence()).

Value

An object of class bmm_report_methods, a list with

  • paragraph: the drafted text, one string;

  • formula: the bmm formula with its constants, one line per parameter (empty without the "model" section);

  • references: the references, numbered by position;

  • notes: what you have to check or add, not meant for the paper;

  • sections: the sections drafted, in order.

print() shows all of it; format() returns the paragraph, the formula and the numbered references as one string to paste into a document. The references keep the Markdown emphasis marks that citation() writes (_journal_, *volume*): Quarto renders them as italics; in Word, remove them.

Details

Every value in the text is read from the fit, and every reference comes from the model's constructor (see model_citation()) or from citation() of an installed package. Nothing else enters the text:

  • The versions are those the fit stores. The R version is stored by fits made with bmm 1.5.0 or later; for older fits it is left out and a note asks you to add it.

  • The references are those of the packages installed now. A note says when an installed version differs from the version the fit was made with.

  • The convergence sentence gives numbers, not verdicts: the largest R-hat and the smallest bulk and tail effective sample sizes over all estimated parameters (constants, lp__ and lprior excluded), and the number of divergent transitions after warmup. Where the summary of brms would warn (an R-hat above 1.05 among the parameters it shows, or a divergent transition), a note says so.

  • For algorithms other than "sampling", the convergence sentence is replaced by a note, as there are no Markov chains to diagnose.

In the text, the numbers in square brackets refer to the reference list. A model without a reference gets [CITATION NEEDED] in that list.

See also

report_convergence(), prior_info(), model_citation()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # identical(Sys.getenv("BMM_EXAMPLES"), "true")
fit <- bmm(
  bmf(c ~ 0 + set_size, kappa ~ 1),
  data = oberauer_lin_2017,
  model = sdm(resp_error = "dev_rad")
)
report_methods(fit)
report_methods(fit, sections = c("model", "convergence"))
cat(format(report_methods(fit)))
}
